appeal.letter:
Subject: Appeal Against Denial of Claim ID 922fb35e-148d-9e82-e2e4-3102298a68a9 – Request for Reconsideration

Claim Details:  
- Claim ID: 922fb35e-148d-9e82-e2e4-3102298a68a9  
- Patient ID: 922fb35e-148d-9e82-7e65-bfa05e3b3515  
- Patient Name: Agnes Laree Weber  
- Date of Claim Submission: 30 June 2024  
- Total Amount Claimed: INR 342.2  
- Encounter Class: Ambulatory (AMB) – Follow‑up encounter for Essential hypertension  
- Policy: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code SGH‑SILVER) – Coverage effective 3 May 2024  

Grounds for Appeal:  
The denial was based on D03 – Pre‑existing disease waiting period not completed. Under the policy definition, a Pre‑Existing Disease is a condition diagnosed within 48 months prior to the first policy start date. Essential hypertension for the patient was first diagnosed on 31 May 2024, which is after the policy start date of 3 May 2024. Therefore, by definition, it is not a Pre‑Existing Disease and the waiting period does not apply [suraksha_silver_policy#5]. Consequently, the clause that imposes a 36‑month waiting period for Pre‑Existing Diseases is inapplicable to this claim [suraksha_silver_policy#11].

Clinical Necessity:  
Guidelines for essential hypertension recommend regular follow‑up monitoring after diagnosis or a medication change, with reviews every 4–6 weeks until control is achieved and then at 3–6 month intervals. Monitoring includes blood pressure measurement, electrolytes, creatinine, and screening for target‑organ damage, which are essential to prevent serious complications such as stroke, heart failure, and kidney disease [hypertension#3]. The follow‑up encounter submitted in this claim aligns with these medically necessary monitoring requirements.

Reference to Denial Standards:  
According to the insurer’s own denial standards, the burden of proof for applying an exclusion or waiting period rests with the insurer, which must provide documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed before the policy start date. No such evidence has been presented; the medical record clearly shows the diagnosis date as 31 May 2024, after coverage commenced. Hence, the insurer has not met its evidentiary burden [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6].

Specific Request:  
In view of the above, we respectfully request that the denial be withdrawn, the claim be reprocessed, and the amount of INR 342.2 be paid in full under the terms of the Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

### 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
Pre-Existing Disease means any condition, ailment, injury or disease that was diagnosed by a physician, or for which medical advice or treatment was received, within 48 months PRIOR TO the first policy start date. citations.section: Essential Hypertension — Diagnosis and Monitoring > Medical Necessity of Monitoring
citations.quote:
## Medical Necessity of Monitoring
After diagnosis or a medication change, review every 4–6 weeks until controlled, then every 3–6 months. Monitoring includes blood pressure measurement, electrolytes and creatinine, and screening for target-organ damage (ECG, urine albumin). Regular monitoring prevents stroke, heart failure and kidney disease.

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.
